about_me.title: About Me
about_me.text: I'm a **3rd-year cybersecurity student** focused on low-level systems, Linux, and open‑source software. I organize my learning with the **PARA method** in Obsidian and believe in building things to truly understand them — whether it's a memory allocator, a shell, or an ELF loader. I enjoy learning how things work under the hood, from syscalls to memory management, and applying that knowledge in practical projects.

philosophy.title: Philosophy
philosophy.text: I believe in **building things, not just reading about them**. Free resources first, simplicity, and strong foundations. I prefer tools that respect user freedom, transparency, and performance. If you haven't triggered a segfault today, you didn't learn enough.

journey.title: Learning Journey
journey.subtitle: From OS internals to web security — a sequential roadmap

phase_0.title: Operating Systems
phase_0.description: Deep-diving OS internals — processes, virtual memory, syscalls, synchronization, and file systems. Runs alongside Phase 1 and provides the foundation for everything that follows.

phase_1.title: Reverse Engineering
phase_1.description: Read and understand compiled binaries (ELF), master debuggers like GDB and Ghidra, analyze malware-like samples, and build a foundation for exploitation.

phase_2.title: Binary Exploitation
phase_2.description: Exploit memory corruption vulnerabilities — stack overflows, heap exploits, format strings, and ROP chains to gain code execution.

phase_3.title: Web Pentesting
phase_3.description: Identify and exploit common web vulnerabilities — SQL injection, XSS, SSRF, authentication flaws, and API pentesting.
